svg.title: Halo architecture
svg.desc: A Chrome extension on the Meet tab streams call and mic audio to a local FastAPI backend. The backend turns speech into attributed turns, live points, urgency tags, coach tips and end-of-meeting notes, all on Meta models, stores everything in local SQLite, and serves the notes page.
svg.text: Halo: from a spoken sentence to a note
Everything runs on this PC except the model calls, and every model is a Meta model. Green is the live path; hover a box for details.

g.title: Reads Meet's DOM (data-participant-id, name spans, the speaking highlight). The only module that knows Meet.
Draws glass bubbles on the speaker's tile (Frame mode) or beside the face with the name above the head (Halo mode). textContent only: Meet enforces Trusted Types.
Sends the speaking tile's frame to the local SAM 3.1 worker; frames never leave this PC.
Pairing with a one-time 6-digit code; subject, agenda, roles; Start is the user gesture tabCapture needs.
Mints the meeting id, captures tab and mic audio as 16 kHz PCM, holds the only socket, resends anything not ACKed.
The backend's only front door: /ws, /pair. Validates every envelope against /contracts, dedupes by id, ACKs on the socket.
Call audio in diarization mode, your mic in endpointing mode ('you'); finals only.
Joins each final turn with Meet's speaking highlight (lag knob, locks after 3 agreeing turns).
Attributed turns to points: kind, urgency, exact quote. Triggers at the speaker's pause.
One batched call every 10 s re-checks kind and urgency. A user re-tag always wins.
Reads the meeting so far on new words (at most every 8 s) or a 15 s silence; filters repeats and talk-over alerts when alone.
The only place model calls are made: schema-checked JSON, one retry, per-call failover, engine recorded on every result.

svg.text: In-process event bus: every message is a typed envelope, checked against /contracts

g.title: Appends every accepted envelope (WAL); views for current points and effective tags.
webm chunks to data/recordings with a time index, so every item can jump to its moment.
On meeting.ended: one schema-checked Spark call; falls back to the live points if it fails twice.
Serves the notes page and its JSON; Ask expands the question into EN + AR keywords, scores passages, Spark answers with citations.
Nothing is hosted. Delete the folder to wipe everything.
g.text: events.sqlite, recordings/, health.json (every 5 s), alerts.jsonl, backend.log

g.title: The only thing modules share. Import-linter fails the build if one module imports another.
g.text: one JSON Schema per message; Python + TypeScript types generated

g.title: muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, realtime WebSocket, two sessions per meeting.
Runs every text call when no Spark Open key is set; otherwise the per-call failover.
meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026; first choice for text calls when its key is set.
Finds the speaker's face so the name sits above the head. About 220 ms per frame on an RTX 3080 Ti.
g.text: open weights on your NVIDIA GPU

svg.text: speaking tile frame, then a face box (Halo mode only)

g.title: Hub (offscreen document) and Gateway. Pairing: a one-time 6-digit code; Origin pinned to the extension id.
g.text: to the backend: audio frames (16 kHz
PCM, call + mic) and typed envelopes,
each ACKed and resent until it is;
back: points, tags, coach tips, live

g.title: rig/fakes, rig/fake_meet, rig/replayer, backend/halo/coach/eval. CI runs them on every pull request.

wire protocols, a fake Meet page that
loads the real extension, a replay rig,

g.title: Ask answers from your past meetings with the exact stored lines it used.
Urgent / Medium / Later with owners and email links; every item jumps to its transcript line and recording moment.
Countable facts about the viewer only, with one thing to try next call.
